title: Israel halts the entry of all goods and humanitarian aid into Gaza
body:
On Sunday 2 March 2025, the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel was suspending the entry of all goods and humanitarian supplies into the Gaza Strip. The announcement came one day after the first phase of the ceasefire that began on 19 January 2025 expired on 1 March.

Netanyahu's office said Hamas had refused a proposal by US envoy Steve Witkoff for a six-week extension of the ceasefire, a plan Israel said it had accepted. The office warned that if Hamas continued to reject the extension there would be further consequences. The second and third phases of the original agreement were meant to cover Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction under the supervision of Egypt, Qatar and the United Nations, but negotiations had made little progress.

A Hamas spokesperson called the move a violation of the ceasefire agreement and asked mediators from Egypt, Qatar and the United States to intervene. Hamas insisted that phase two, including further prisoner exchanges and an Israeli withdrawal, must proceed as originally negotiated, and urged the international community to pressure Israel to lift the restrictions.

The United Nations said more than 10,000 aid trucks had entered Gaza between 19 January and 6 February 2025. According to the Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry, at least 48,365 Palestinians had been killed in Gaza since the war began on 7 October 2023. The halt on aid remained in place until Israel allowed a limited quantity of supplies in during May 2025.
